generalization_failure_diagnosis.finding: CRITICAL: Model failed on test set despite perfect val performance.
generalization_failure_diagnosis.root_cause: FOR-2sec codec confound: training FAKE files are MP3-sourced (file*.mp3.wav_16k...) while test FAKE files are WAV-sourced (file*.wav_16k...). The model learned to detect MP3 codec artefacts, not TTS synthesis signatures. This is a documented dataset design flaw in FOR-2sec.
evidence: Test FAKE file suffix: .wav_16k.wav_norm... (WAV origin, no MP3 codec artefacts)
Feature direction reversal: mfcc_delta_4_std Cohen_d train=+0.89 vs test=-2.20
Test class separability is HIGHER than train (ratio 1.46x) but in opposite direction
Retraining on combined train+val does not help (same confound in both)
p(FAKE) on test: FAKE=0.266 REAL=0.278 — model is effectively blind
generalization_failure_diagnosis.implication_for_adis: This model MUST NOT be integrated into ADIS as-is. It would classify MP3-compressed audio as FAKE regardless of whether it is synthesised. Recommended path: retrain on a codec-balanced dataset or apply codec-blind feature engineering (e.g. cepstral mean subtraction).
recommended_next_steps: 1. Codec-blind retraining: apply CMS (cepstral mean subtraction) to neutralise channel/codec effects
2. Dataset augmentation: apply MP3 re-encoding at various bitrates to both REAL and FAKE during training
3. Alternative dataset: use In-The-Wild or ASVspoof which do not have this codec confound
4. Feature subset: exclude features known to carry codec artefacts (low-frequency MFCCs, spectral flatness)
